new.s: In the Gupta revenue system, 'bhaga', the main land revenue, was the king's share of the produce. What share did the law books prescribe?
new.x: Bhaga was the king's share of produce and the main land revenue; the law books prescribed one-sixth. Actual rates in the sources vary (1/4 to 1/6, about 1/7), but one-half, one-third and one-tenth are not the prescribed share.

new.s: Harshavardhana is also known by which of the following titles?
new.x: Harsha bore the title Siladitya (APPSC G1 2012) and also Sakalottarapathanatha, lord of all North India. Vikramaditya was the title of Chandragupta II, Paramesvara was taken by Pulakesin II after defeating Harsha, and Shakraditya was Kumaragupta I.

new.s: The Vardhana dynasty of Thanesar, to which Harsha belonged, is also named after its founder. Who was he?
new.x: The line is called the Pushyabhuti dynasty after its founder Pushyabhuti (BPSC 2022 key); its rulers were once Gupta feudatories. Grahavarman was a Maukhari, Vindhyashakti founded the Vakatakas, and Bhaskaravarman ruled Kamarupa.
